An initiative only by young people
2740.e: With a cantonal initiative, a canton can make a proposal to the Confederation. Parliament then decides whether to take it up.
2740.m: A canton can make proposals with a cantonal initiative.

2757.q: What is a municipal office building?
a: The building where the municipality's administration works
2757.e: In the municipal office building, people work who look after things in the village or town. You can apply for a passport there, for example.
2757.m: The municipal administration works in the municipal office building.

2765.q: How can advertising influence the way you spend money?
a: It can create wants that lead to spontaneous, unplanned purchases
Advertising has no effect on purchases
Advertising only informs about legal rules
2765.e: Advertising is designed to create wants and encourage you to buy, even if you do not really need the product. Thinking critically helps you stick to your budget.

a: An object with such strong gravity that not even light can escape
A hole in the Earth’s atmosphere
2776.e: A black hole often forms when a very massive star collapses in on itself at the end of its life. Its pull is so strong that not even light can escape it.
2776.m: Black holes let no light escape.

2779.q: What does it mean to buy something on credit or in instalments?
a: You pay for the product in several parts over time, often with extra costs
You pay the full price in cash straight away
You get the product as a present
You swap it for another product
2779.e: When paying in instalments, you do not pay everything at once but in parts. There are often extra costs or interest, which makes the product more expensive in the end.
2779.m: Paying in instalments can cost more.

2782.q: How endangered is the African wild dog according to the IUCN Red List?
a: It is only known in zoos
2782.e: The IUCN classes it as “endangered”. There are only a few thousand animals left.
2782.m: The African wild dog is endangered.

2787.q: Roughly how often a year can Swiss people go to the polls?
2787.e: In Switzerland there are usually four voting dates a year. People can then decide on various questions.
2787.m: There are usually four voting dates a year.

a: An organisation that connects the police forces of different countries
2819.e: Interpol helps police forces from different countries work together, for example when searching for criminals across borders. Its headquarters are in France.
2819.m: Interpol connects police forces around the world.

a: An office of a country abroad
2826.e: A consulate is an office of a country abroad. It helps, for example, if someone has lost their passport.

2841.q: In which habitats can a leopard be found?
2841.e: Leopards are very adaptable. They live in savannahs, forests, mountains and sometimes even close to cities.

2861.q: In which season do most flowers in Switzerland bloom for the first time?
2861.e: In spring it gets warmer and lighter. Many plants wake up from their winter rest and start to bloom.
2861.m: In spring the plants wake up.

2888.q: What does the abbreviation “EU” stand for?
2888.e: The EU is a group of countries in Europe. They work together on issues such as trade, the environment and travel.

2891.q: What does the law of the lever say, put simply?
a: Effort times effort arm equals load times load arm
The shorter the lever, the less force you need
2891.e: With a lever: the longer the effort arm compared with the load arm, the less force you need to use. That is why long seesaws are easier to work than short ones.
2891.m: A long lever arm saves force.

2896.q: What is the opposite of a dictatorship?
2896.e: In a democracy the people have a say in who governs. That is the opposite of a dictatorship, where one person decides alone.
2896.m: Democracy is the opposite of dictatorship.

2900.q: What is an election ballot paper?
a: A paper on which you tick names for an election
2900.e: The election ballot paper lists the names of people or parties. You tick who you want to elect.
2900.m: On the election ballot paper you choose people.

a: A very cold continent at the South Pole
A warm continent at the equator
An ocean near the North Pole
2901.e: Antarctica lies at the Earth’s South Pole and is mostly covered with thick ice. It is almost always very cold there.
2901.m: Antarctica is at the South Pole and is freezing cold.

2914.q: On which river does the old Landhaus in the town of Solothurn stand?
2914.e: The Landhaus is an old building right on the bank of the Aare. In the past, goods from the boats were stored there; today it hosts parties and concerts.
2914.m: The Landhaus in Solothurn stands on the Aare.

a: A friendship between two municipalities in different countries
A football club with players from many countries
2938.e: Two municipalities in different countries can form a partnership to visit each other and exchange ideas. In this way people from different cultures get to know each other.
2938.m: Town twinning links municipalities across borders.

2953.q: The scientific name of the African wild dog means roughly “painted wolf”. Why does that fit?
2953.e: The wild dog's coat has patches of black, yellow, brown and white. It looks as if someone has painted the animal.

2964.q: What are the coins worth less than one franc called?
2964.e: In Switzerland the small coins are called rappen (centimes in French). 100 rappen make one franc.

a: A thinker who had new ideas about a fair society
2977.e: Karl Marx was a German thinker in the 19th century. His ideas became the basis of communism.
2977.m: Karl Marx thought about a fairer world.

2978.q: In which cities does the European Parliament mainly meet?
2978.e: The European Parliament has its main seat in Strasbourg but often also meets in Brussels. There elected members represent the citizens of the EU countries.
2978.m: The EU Parliament meets in Strasbourg and Brussels.

2994.q: What do you call the movable connection between two bones?
2994.e: Joints connect bones and make movement possible. Cartilage, ligaments and fluid make sure they work well.
2994.m: Joints connect bones so they can move.

2995.q: What is the small device on a bike called that makes electricity for the light from the movement of the wheel?
2995.e: A dynamo makes electricity from the turning of the wheel. This lets the bike light shine without a battery.
2995.m: The dynamo turns movement into electricity.

3001.e: In electoral fraud votes are manipulated or miscounted so that the desired candidate wins. In dictatorships this is a common way of staying in power.
3001.m: False votes fake a real election.

3025.q: What do some dictators like to build to look powerful?
a: Huge statues and pictures of themselves.
3025.e: Big monuments and pictures are meant to show how strong and important the ruler supposedly is. This is called a personality cult.

a: A part of Switzerland with its own government
3057.e: Switzerland is made up of many cantons. Each canton has its own laws and its own government.
3057.m: A canton is a part of Switzerland.

3060.q: What colour is the fur of a typical leopard?
3060.e: A typical leopard has yellowish to golden brown fur with dark rosettes. The belly is lighter.
3060.m: Leopard fur is golden brown with rosettes.

3075.q: What does the organisation Amnesty International work for?
a: Respect for human rights around the world
Peace between the EU and NATO
3075.e: Amnesty International is an independent organisation that works for human rights and makes abuses public. For example, it collects signatures for people in prison.
3075.m: Amnesty International fights for human rights.

3087.q: On which day of the week do Christians usually meet for a church service?
3087.e: Many Christians see Sunday as a special day. They often go to church and rest.
3087.m: Sunday is the Christian holy day of the week.

3127.q: Why do many dictators have a very large army?
a: To protect their power and intimidate critics.
3127.e: A large army helps the dictator stay in power. It can stop protests and spread fear.
3127.m: Large armies keep dictators in power.

3133.q: What is it called when bees carry pollen from one flower to another?
3133.e: When bees collect nectar, pollen sticks to them, and they carry it to the next flower. This allows plants to produce seeds.

3135.q: What makes the European Economic Area (EEA) different from the EU?
a: The EEA allows access to the single market without being an EU member
The EEA has its own army
The EEA is bigger than the EU
The EEA consists only of Switzerland
3135.e: Countries such as Norway are in the EEA without being EU members. Switzerland belongs neither to the EU nor to the EEA, but has its own agreements with the EU.
3135.m: The EEA allows market access without joining the EU.

3140.q: What do young people do in a youth parliament?
a: They talk about politics and bring in ideas
They train for a sports competition
3140.e: In a youth parliament, young people can have their say, even before they are allowed to vote. This way they practise democracy.
3140.m: In a youth parliament, young people practise politics.

3158.q: What do you call someone who is locked up because of their opinions?
3158.e: Political prisoners are in prison because they spoke their minds openly. This happens mainly in dictatorships.
3158.m: Political prisoners are jailed for their opinions.

3159.q: What does the ‘double majority’ mean for a change to the Federal Constitution?
a: It needs both a majority of the voters and a majority of the cantons
It needs twice as many votes as usual
Only the Federal Council decides twice
3159.e: For changes to the constitution, a simple majority of the voters is not enough. A majority of the cantons must also agree.
3159.m: Changing the constitution needs a majority of the people and of the cantons.

3173.q: In which year did Solothurn become a member of the Old Swiss Confederacy?
3173.e: Solothurn joined the Old Swiss Confederacy in 1481, together with the town of Fribourg.
3173.m: In 1481, Solothurn became part of the Confederation.

3177.q: Which statement about the leopard compared with the lion and the tiger is true?
a: It is smaller than the lion and the tiger
It is bigger than the tiger
It is the biggest cat in the world
It is the same size as a lynx
3177.e: The leopard is a medium-sized big cat. Lions and tigers are much heavier.
3177.m: The leopard is smaller than the lion and the tiger.

3179.q: Which South-East Asian country is still ruled by a communist party today?
3179.e: Laos became communist in 1975 and has since been ruled by the Lao People's Revolutionary Party. Like Vietnam and China, it is a one-party state.
3179.m: Laos is still ruled by communists today.

3222.q: How many cubs does a female leopard usually have per litter?
3222.e: A female leopard usually has two to three cubs, rarely only one. The cubs are born blind.
3222.m: Leopards usually have two to three cubs.

3224.q: Why are there different seasons on Earth?
a: Because the Earth’s axis is tilted relative to the sun
Because the Earth is sometimes nearer to and sometimes further from the sun
Because the sun goes round the Earth
Because the moon blocks the sunlight
3224.e: The Earth’s axis is slightly tilted. As a result, the sun shines more or less strongly on the northern and southern hemispheres depending on the time of year.
3224.m: The tilt of the Earth’s axis causes the seasons.

3250.q: Which animal miaows and is one of the most popular pets in Switzerland?
3250.e: The cat is the most common pet in Switzerland. Many cats go outdoors and hunt little mice.
3250.m: The cat is a popular Swiss pet.

3260.q: Which animal has a very long neck so it can eat the highest leaves?
3260.e: The giraffe is the tallest land animal in the world and has a neck up to two metres long. This lets it reach leaves high up in the treetops.
3260.m: The giraffe has the longest neck.

a: A popular uprising against the communist government was crushed by Soviet troops
3265.e: In autumn 1956 many people in Hungary rose up against communist rule. The Soviet Union sent tanks to end the uprising.
3265.m: In 1956 the Soviets crushed the Hungarian Uprising.

3275.q: What stands up on your skin when you get goose bumps?
3275.e: When it is cold, tiny muscles in the skin tighten. Then the tiny hairs stand up, and the skin looks like that of a plucked goose.
3275.m: With goose bumps, the tiny hairs stand up.

3279.q: Which big cat is the fastest over short distances?
3279.e: The cheetah is the fastest land animal in the world and briefly reaches over 100 km/h. Leopards, lions and tigers are much slower.
3279.m: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

3290.q: What do the annual rings in a tree trunk show?
a: They show the age of the tree
They show how much rain there will be tomorrow
They show the size of the leaves
3290.e: Each annual ring comes from one year’s growth, wider in spring and narrower in autumn. If you count the rings, you know how old the tree is.
3290.m: Annual rings reveal the age of a tree.

3293.q: What is meant by a monoculture in farming?
a: Growing just one plant species over a large area
Growing many different plant species together
A forest with many animal species
3293.e: In a monoculture only one plant species is grown over large areas, for example only maize. This can exhaust the soil and reduce biodiversity.
3293.m: In a monoculture only one plant species is grown.

3328.q: Since which year has Switzerland been a member of the UN?
3328.e: For a long time Switzerland stayed out of the UN because of its neutrality. Only after a referendum did it officially join in 2002.

3332.q: How long is the deadline for calling an optional referendum against a federal law?
3332.e: After a law is published, its opponents have 100 days to collect signatures.
3332.m: You have 100 days for a referendum.

3333.q: What do you call the direct change from solid to gas without a substance becoming liquid?
3333.e: In sublimation, a solid turns directly into a gas, like dry ice, for example, which simply disappears into the air. There is no liquid stage in between.
3333.m: In sublimation, a solid turns directly into a gas.

3338.q: What was the aim of the Kyoto Protocol?
a: To commit countries to reducing greenhouse gases
To redraw the borders between states
To regulate world trade in oil
To secure peace between Japan and the USA
3338.e: The Kyoto Protocol was an international agreement under which industrial states were to cut their greenhouse gas emissions. It was an important forerunner of the later Paris Climate Agreement.
3338.m: Kyoto committed states to protecting the climate.

3341.q: What do you hear music and voices with?
3341.e: Your ears catch sound waves and pass them on to the brain. There they become sounds and words.

3356.q: What is meant by the greenhouse effect?
a: Gases in the atmosphere keep heat on Earth
The sun comes closer to the Earth every year
It makes the Earth spin faster
3356.e: Certain gases such as CO2 let sunlight through to the Earth but hold back the heat radiation that the Earth gives off again. Without this natural effect, it would be much colder on Earth.
3356.m: Greenhouse gases keep heat in the atmosphere.

3360.q: What does the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), based in Geneva, deal with?
a: Worldwide rules for telecommunications and the internet
3360.e: The ITU coordinates technical standards for telephone, radio and the internet worldwide. It is one of the oldest international organisations and is based in Geneva.
3360.m: The ITU sets the rules for communications technology worldwide.

a: The highest law of a state, which sets out rights and limits on power.
3374.e: A constitution sets out how a state is organised and what rights citizens have. In dictatorships the constitution is often ignored or changed.

3422.q: How did the rule of the Romanian dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu end?
a: In 1989 he was overthrown in a revolution and executed
He resigned voluntarily and went into exile
He ruled until he died of old age
The EU made him an honorary citizen
3422.e: At the end of 1989 there was a violent uprising against Ceaușescu in Romania. He and his wife were shot after a short trial.

3426.q: In which year did East and West Germany become one country again?
3426.e: One year after the fall of the Wall, the GDR and the Federal Republic of Germany were reunited. That was on 3 October 1990.

3450.q: Which organ produces the hormone insulin?
3450.e: The pancreas makes insulin, which lowers the blood sugar level. It also produces digestive enzymes.

3470.q: Which animal hops on strong back legs and carries its young in a pouch?
3470.e: The kangaroo lives in Australia and can jump very far with its strong legs. The young grow up in their mother's pouch.
3470.m: The kangaroo carries its babies in a pouch.

a: A group of the 20 most important economies in the world
A UN department for environmental issues
3482.e: In the G20 the governments of the biggest economies meet to talk about the economy, the climate and other global issues. Switzerland is not one of the permanent members.
3482.m: The G20 are the 20 biggest economic powers.

3490.q: Which country calls itself the “Land of the Thunder Dragon” and still shows the dragon on its flag today?
3490.e: Bhutan is also called the “Land of the Thunder Dragon”. The yellow and orange halves of the flag stand for worldly and spiritual power.
3490.m: Bhutan's flag shows a thunder dragon.

3528.q: What was the Reichstag fire in 1933?
a: A fire in the German parliament building that the Nazis used for their own ends.
A festival planned by the Nazis.
A natural event with no consequences.
3528.e: After the Reichstag fire the National Socialists blamed their opponents and severely restricted basic rights. This helped them expand their power.
3528.m: The fire served as an excuse to seize power.

3537.q: What is World Refugee Day for?
a: To remember people who have had to flee from war or danger
To celebrate new countries on the map
To remember the founding of the EU
3537.e: On World Refugee Day, people all over the world think of those who have had to leave their homes. It is meant to show that refugees need help and protection.

a: A group in which several countries work together
A club for children in a town
A shop that sells goods from abroad
A school with children from many countries
3582.e: In an international organisation, countries work together on issues such as peace, health or the environment. The UN and the EU are examples.

3623.q: What do the hammer and sickle on communist flags mean?
a: They stand for workers and farmers
They stand for kings and nobles
They stand for soldiers and generals
They stand for teachers and pupils
3623.e: The hammer stands for the workers in the factories, the sickle for the farmers in the countryside. Together they were supposed to build society.
3623.m: The hammer and sickle stand for workers and farmers.

3625.q: How does a leopard typically hunt?
a: It sneaks up and makes a short dash
It chases its prey for hours
3625.e: The leopard creeps as close as possible to its prey. Then it overpowers it with a short sprint.
3625.m: Leopards sneak up on their prey.

3634.q: Which animal is often called the “king of the animals” and lives in Africa?
3634.e: Because of its strength and courage, the lion is seen as the king of the animals. Lions live in groups called prides.
3634.m: The lion is seen as the king of the animals.

3642.q: What is the celebration called when a Jewish boy becomes a religious adult at 13?
3642.e: At his Bar Mitzvah the boy reads from the Torah in public for the first time. After that, in the Jewish faith, he is seen as religiously responsible.
3642.m: The Bar Mitzvah celebrates becoming a religious adult.

3648.q: What happens to your skin if you stay in the sun too long?
3648.e: Too much sun damages the skin and makes it red and sore. That is why sun cream is important.
3648.m: Too much sun hurts your skin.

3651.q: What was the “Cultural Revolution” in China?
a: A campaign by Mao against supposed enemies and old traditions.
3651.e: During the Cultural Revolution millions of people were persecuted, humiliated or killed because they supposedly did not think in a “revolutionary” enough way. Education and culture also suffered badly.
3651.m: The Cultural Revolution persecuted supposed enemies.

3653.q: Which animal is the biggest animal in the world and lives in the sea?
3653.e: The blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived on Earth. It can grow over 30 metres long.
3653.m: The blue whale is the biggest animal of all.

3657.q: What does it show when a wild dog opens its mouth slightly and approaches others in a friendly way?
a: It is showing affection to the pack
It wants to run away at once
3657.e: Wild dogs often greet each other with sounds and body contact. This strengthens the bond within the pack.
3657.m: Greetings strengthen the bond in the pack.

3681.q: Why does a piece of wood float on water?
a: Because wood is lighter than the same amount of water
Because wood is made of water
3681.e: Wood has a lower density than water, which is why it floats on top. Heavy materials such as stone sink because they are denser than water.
3681.m: Lighter things float, heavier things sink.

3687.q: What job do the intervertebral discs have in the spine?
a: They cushion knocks between the vertebrae
3687.e: Discs sit between the vertebrae and act like shock absorbers. They make the spine flexible and protect it.

3718.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
a: Mass stays the same everywhere, weight depends on gravity
Mass and weight are exactly the same
Weight stays the same everywhere, mass changes
3718.e: The mass of a body is the same everywhere in the universe, wherever it is. Weight, on the other hand, depends on gravity, which is weaker on the Moon, for example.
3718.m: Mass stays the same, weight changes.

3728.q: Roughly how fast can an African wild dog run when hunting?
a: Up to about 60 kilometres per hour
3728.e: Over a short distance it reaches about 60 kilometres per hour. That is much faster than an everyday bike ride.

3761.q: What is the name of the hilly area in the canton of Solothurn with many small villages?
3761.e: The Bucheggberg is a rural area in the canton of Solothurn with fields, forests and small villages. The Emmental and the Seeland are in the canton of Bern, the Toggenburg in St Gallen.
3761.m: The Bucheggberg is a rural region in the canton of Solothurn.

3766.q: What do you measure when you take someone's blood pressure?
a: How strongly the blood pushes against the walls of the vessels
How much oxygen is in the blood
3766.e: Blood pressure shows how strongly the blood pushes against the walls of the arteries. It is given as two numbers, for example 120 over 80.
3766.m: Blood pressure is the pressure of the blood in the vessels.

a: Areas of the Earth with a similar, typical climate
Areas at the same height above sea level
3776.e: The Earth is roughly divided into tropical, temperate and polar climate zones. They differ mainly in temperature and precipitation.
3776.m: Climate zones show the typical weather conditions of a region.

3792.q: What colour is the tip of the tail of many African wild dogs?
3792.e: The white tail tip works like a signal. It helps the animals keep each other in sight when hunting in tall grass.
3792.m: The white tail tip helps them find their way.

a: Supplying West Berlin by aeroplane during a Soviet blockade
A bridge that linked East and West Berlin
3804.e: When the Soviet Union blocked the land routes to West Berlin, the Western powers supplied the city from the air for almost a year. This meant West Berlin could be held.
3804.m: The Airlift supplied West Berlin from the air.

3808.q: In which country is Kruger National Park, where wild dogs live?
3808.e: Wild dogs live in Kruger National Park in South Africa. It is one of the best-known protected areas in Africa.
3808.m: Wild dogs live in Kruger National Park.

3827.e: UNESCO is a UN organisation that protects schools, research and important cultural sites. For example, it draws up the World Heritage List.
3827.m: UNESCO protects education, science and culture.

3840.q: Which animal is known for being slow and carries its shell on its back like a house?
3840.e: The tortoise always carries its hard shell with it like a house. When in danger, it can hide its head and legs completely inside.
3840.m: The tortoise carries its house with it.

3859.q: What does it mean when a proposal in a vote is ‘thrown out’?
3859.e: If more people say No than Yes, a proposal is thrown out, that is, rejected. Then everything stays as it was.

3874.q: What happens if you always spend all your pocket money straight away?
a: You have nothing left when you need something later
You automatically get more pocket money
Nothing, that is always a good idea
3874.e: If you spend everything at once, you have no money left for later wishes or emergencies. It is worth putting something aside.
3874.m: If you spend everything, nothing is left.

3878.q: What is the International Space Station (ISS)?
a: A crewed research laboratory in orbit around the Earth
An uncrewed satellite for watching the weather
A space probe on its way to Mars
3878.e: The ISS orbits the Earth at about 400 kilometres up and is permanently occupied by international teams of astronauts. Many scientific experiments in weightlessness are carried out there.
3878.m: The ISS is a crewed laboratory in space.

3882.q: What do you need your muscles for?
3882.e: Muscles tighten and in this way move your bones. Without them you could neither walk nor grab things.

3892.q: Which disease, which can also affect pet dogs, is dangerous for wild dogs?
3892.e: Diseases such as rabies and distemper can be passed from pet dogs to wild dogs. This can threaten whole packs.
3892.m: Pet dogs can pass diseases on to wild dogs.

a: A paper that shows you are allowed to vote
3913.e: The voting card arrives at home by post. You need it to take part in a vote.
3913.m: The voting card shows that you are allowed to vote.

3916.q: How do you calculate the electrical power of an appliance?
a: Power is voltage divided by resistance
3916.e: The formula P = U x I tells you how much electrical energy is converted per unit of time. Power is given in watts.

3927.q: Which animal can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
3927.e: The coat of arms of Appenzell Innerrhoden shows a black bear on a white background. The bear comes from the Abbey of St Gallen, which Appenzell used to belong to.
3927.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden has a bear on its coat of arms.

3939.q: Who rules communist North Korea today?
a: A president elected by the people
3939.e: Kim Jong-un is the ruler of North Korea. His family has already ruled the country for three generations.

3942.q: Which way does a brown trout usually face in a stream?
a: With its head against the current
With its head in the direction of the current
3942.e: This way fresh water reaches its gills and food drifts straight towards it. With a few flicks of its fins it stays in place.

3944.q: What are Swiss cantons allowed to do in foreign policy?
a: Make their own agreements with neighbouring regions abroad in certain areas
Decide on war and peace on their own
Take foreign policy away from the Confederation completely
3944.e: Border cantons may, for example, make agreements on cooperation with neighbouring regions in France, Germany or Italy. But major foreign policy remains a matter for the Confederation.
3944.m: Cantons may work across borders to a limited extent.

3947.q: The picture shows a newly hatched trout with a sac on its belly. What is it for?
a: It is a yolk sac and provides food
3947.e: The yolk sac contains nutrients. The little fish lives on it for the first few weeks.
3947.m: The yolk sac feeds the young fish.

3972.q: What is meant by coming to terms with the past after a dictatorship ends?
a: Society working through the injustice that was committed.
A ban on talking about the past.
3972.e: After a dictatorship ends, societies often try to investigate crimes, compensate victims and hold perpetrators to account. This is meant to help prevent similar injustice in future.
3972.m: Working through the past prevents new injustice.

3974.q: What does the physical quantity density describe?
a: How much mass there is in a certain volume
How heavy an object is on the Moon
3974.e: Density tells you how much mass fits into a certain space, for example grams per cubic centimetre. Lead has a high density, polystyrene a very low one.

3983.q: What is the name of a well-known old tower in the old town of Solothurn?
3983.e: The Riedholz Tower is one of the old defensive towers that were once part of Solothurn's town wall. The Zytglogge and the Käfigturm are in Bern, the Munot in Schaffhausen.
3983.m: The Riedholz Tower was part of the old town wall.

3997.q: Why does a red apple look red to us?
a: It reflects red light and absorbs the other colours
It contains red dye that glows by itself
It changes the light into red waves
3997.e: White light contains all colours. The apple absorbs most colours and reflects only the red light, which then enters our eyes.
3997.m: We see the colour that is reflected.

4001.q: Roughly how many countries belong to the European Union?
4001.e: The European Union has around 27 member countries. Switzerland does not belong to it but works together with the EU.
4001.m: The EU has around 27 member countries.

4016.q: What happens in a series circuit if one bulb breaks?
a: All the other bulbs go out too
Only the broken bulb stays dark, the rest keep shining
4016.e: In a series circuit there is only one single path for the current. If this path is broken at one point, the current cannot flow at all any more.
4016.m: One broken bulb stops the whole series.

4018.q: On which continents do wild leopards live?
4018.e: Leopards live in Africa and parts of Asia. There are no wild leopards in America or Australia.
4018.m: Leopards live in Africa and Asia.

4031.q: Roughly how long does an African wild dog live in the wild?
4031.e: In the wild they usually live to around 10 to 12 years. But many die earlier from disease or other dangers.
4031.m: Wild dogs live to about ten years.

a: A Swiss app for paying without cash using a smartphone
A Swiss bank that only serves young people
4032.e: Twint is a payment app widely used in Switzerland. You can use it to shop with your phone or send money to friends. The money is taken from the linked bank account.

4034.q: What is the process called in which plants make food using sunlight?
4034.e: In photosynthesis, plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make sugar as food. Oxygen is produced as a by-product.
4034.m: In photosynthesis plants make sugar using light.

4049.q: What job does the appendix probably have?
a: It probably supports the immune system in the gut
4049.e: Today the appendix is thought to be a possible store for useful gut bacteria. People used to think it was useless.
4049.m: The appendix probably helps the gut bacteria.

4050.q: Which UN organisation makes sure that people in the world have enough to eat?
4050.e: The FAO is the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. It helps to fight hunger in the world.
4050.m: The FAO works to make sure there is enough food for everyone.

4053.q: Which symbol is often linked with Islam?
4053.e: The crescent and star decorate many mosques and the flags of Islamic countries. They have become a well-known sign of Islam.
4053.m: The crescent and star often stand for Islam.

4058.q: How do injured or sick wild dogs often get treated in the pack?
a: They are driven away at once
4058.e: Pack members also share food with sick or old animals. This shows how strong the bond is.
4058.m: Wild dogs look after each other.

4059.q: What happens when you cut your finger slightly and it bleeds a little?
a: The blood helps to close the wound later
The skin stays open for ever
4059.e: Blood contains special substances that can close a wound. A crust forms, and the skin heals underneath it.
4059.m: Blood helps your skin to heal.

4069.q: In which part of Switzerland is the canton of Solothurn?
4069.e: The canton of Solothurn lies in the Swiss Central Plateau, between the Jura and the Alps. It has many hills and forests.
4069.m: Solothurn lies in the Central Plateau of Switzerland.

4099.q: Roughly how long is a female leopard pregnant?
4099.e: Pregnancy lasts around 90 to 105 days. That is about three months.
4099.m: Leopards are pregnant for about three months.

4110.q: What helps to protect the African wild dog?
4110.e: Protected areas preserve habitat, and vaccinations protect against disease. Working with local people also helps.

4146.q: Why is your shadow much shorter at midday than in the evening?
a: Because the sun is high in the sky at midday
Because you walk faster at midday
Because your body gets smaller at midday
Because it is brighter at midday than in the evening
4146.e: When the sun is high in the sky, its rays fall on you more steeply and your shadow is short. In the evening the sun is low, so your shadow is long.
4146.m: A high sun makes short shadows.

4150.q: What does a trout use its swim bladder for?
a: It helps it float at one depth in the water
4150.e: The swim bladder is filled with gas and provides buoyancy. That way the fish can float without much effort.

4154.q: What is a motion in parliament?
a: A binding order to the Federal Council
4154.e: With a motion, members of parliament can oblige the Federal Council to prepare a law or a decision. If both chambers accept the motion, the Federal Council must act.
4154.m: A motion obliges the Federal Council to act.

4155.q: Where do African wild dogs usually give birth to their pups?
a: In a nest made of feathers
4155.e: They often use abandoned burrows of other animals. The pups are safe there.
4155.m: Pups grow up in an underground den.

4170.q: What was the name of the only party allowed in the Soviet Union?
a: Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU)
4170.e: In the Soviet Union, the CPSU was the only party allowed. It controlled the state, the economy and society almost completely.
4170.m: The CPSU was the only party in the USSR.

4181.q: Which organisation uses a light blue flag with a map of the world surrounded by a white olive wreath?
4181.e: The UN flag shows a map of the world framed by two olive branches as a symbol of peace. The UN was founded in 1945 and the flag introduced in 1947.
4181.m: The UN flag stands for peace worldwide.

4186.q: What is the basic principle of a heat pump?
a: It takes heat from the surroundings and releases it in the house
It produces heat directly from electricity by burning
It pumps hot water from the sea into the house
It stores sunlight in a battery
4186.e: A heat pump takes in heat from the air, the ground or the groundwater, even when they are cool. With a little electricity, this heat is then raised to a higher temperature and fed into the house.
4186.m: Heat pumps get heat from the surroundings.

4231.q: What is the protective layer around nerve fibres that speeds up signals called?
4231.e: The myelin sheath wraps around many nerve fibres like insulation. It makes electrical signals travel much faster.

4234.q: Why do you wash your hands before eating?
a: So that no germs get into your mouth
So that your hands get cold
4234.e: There are often invisible germs on your hands. Washing removes them before you eat.
4234.m: Before eating, you wash your hands clean.

a: Support for poorer countries from richer countries and organisations
4241.e: Development cooperation includes financial, technical and staff support so that poorer countries can develop economically and socially. Switzerland does this, among other ways, through the SDC.

a: A machine that turns wind into electricity
4244.e: The wind turns the large blades of the turbine. This turning is then converted into electricity.
4244.m: Wind turns the blades, and the blades make electricity.

a: Messenger substances that send signals to organs through the blood
Cells that are only found in the brain
4251.e: Hormones are made by glands and released into the blood. They control, for example, growth and metabolism.
4251.m: Hormones are messengers in the blood.

a: A research centre where countries study physics together
A football stadium for world cups
4277.e: At CERN researchers from many countries work together to learn more about how the world is made. It lies partly in Switzerland and partly in France.
4277.m: At CERN many countries do research together.

a: A leopard or jaguar with black fur
4298.e: Black panthers are usually leopards or jaguars whose bodies make especially large amounts of dark pigment. In slanting light you can often still see the spots.
4298.m: A black panther is usually a black leopard or jaguar.

a: Money borrowed from a bank to buy something like furniture or a car, which must be paid back with interest
A loan you only get for food
Money the state gives to all young people
4301.e: With a consumer loan you borrow money for purchases and later have to pay it back with interest. This can quickly lead to debt if you are not careful.
4301.m: A consumer loan must be paid back with interest.

4304.q: What is the name of the well-known mountain pass in the Jura that belongs to the canton of Solothurn?
4304.e: The Passwang lies in the Jura mountains in the canton of Solothurn and is popular with hikers and cyclists. From there you have a great view of the mountains.
4304.m: The Passwang is a pass in the Jura near Solothurn.

4306.q: Which electoral system is mostly used to elect the Council of States?
4306.e: In a majority vote, whoever gets the most votes wins. This is how the Council of States is elected in most cantons.
4306.m: For the Council of States, whoever has the most votes usually wins.

4328.q: How many seasons are there in Switzerland?
4328.e: In Switzerland there are spring, summer, autumn and winter. Each season lasts about three months.
4328.m: There are four seasons a year.

4339.q: In which landscape does the African wild dog live most often?
a: In the high mountains of the Alps
4339.e: It needs open country where it can hunt its prey well. It usually avoids dense rainforests and deserts.
4339.m: Wild dogs need open country for hunting.

4359.q: In which city does the Swiss government, the Federal Council, meet?
4359.e: Bern is Switzerland’s federal city, and the Federal Council works there. The whole country is governed from there.

4366.e: Forests are cleared, and leopards are hunted for their fur. There are also conflicts with people when livestock is killed.
4366.m: Habitat loss and poaching threaten leopards.

4371.q: Who usually has the pups in a pack?
a: All the females at the same time
4371.e: Usually only the highest-ranking pair breeds. The other animals help raise the young.
4371.m: Usually only the leading pair has pups.

4379.q: In the picture a trout is jumping. What does it often do this for?
a: To get over small obstacles and steps
To hunt birds in the air
4379.e: Brown trout can jump over small waterfalls and weirs. Sometimes they also leap for insects.

4388.q: Which animal with big round ears and a colourful coat of yellow, black and white patches can you see in the picture?
4388.e: The African wild dog has an irregular, patchy coat. Each animal has its own pattern, a bit like a fingerprint.
4388.m: Every wild dog has a unique coat pattern.

4408.q: What does opposition mean in politics?
a: People or parties who disagree with the government.
4408.e: An opposition criticises the government and proposes other solutions. In dictatorships the opposition is often banned or persecuted.
4408.m: The opposition thinks differently from the government.

4422.q: What is the booklet called that explains the issues before a vote?
4422.e: Before every vote, all voters receive a booklet explaining the issues. This way they can find out more.
4422.m: The voting booklet explains the issues.

4424.q: What does a solar cell do?
a: It turns sunlight directly into electricity
It stores heat for the night
4424.e: In a solar cell, particles of light hit a special material and free electrons in it. This movement of electrons produces the electric current.
4424.m: Solar cells turn light into electricity.

4425.q: Which sense helps you feel whether something is hot or cold?
a: The sense of touch in your skin
4425.e: In your skin there are tiny sensors that feel warmth, cold and pressure. That is the sense of touch.
4425.m: Your skin feels hot and cold.

4429.q: Apart from light, what else does the sun give the Earth?
4429.e: The sun's rays warm up the Earth. Without this heat, it would be far too cold on Earth for life.
4429.m: The sun brings light and heat.

4456.q: What are the ring-shaped spots in a leopard's fur called?
4456.e: The leopard's spots are arranged in rings and look like little roses. That is why they are called rosettes.
4456.m: Leopards have rosettes in their fur.

4463.q: How can children earn a little money themselves?
a: With small jobs, for example watering the neighbours' flowers
By simply getting it from a cash machine
By asking the municipality for it
4463.e: By helping a little at home or in the neighbourhood, children can earn some extra money. But ask your parents first.
4463.m: Small jobs earn you your own money.

4474.q: Which animal lives in the Swiss Alps, is a good climber and is often confused with the chamois?
4474.e: The ibex and the chamois look alike, but the ibex is much bigger and has much thicker, ridged horns. Both species live above the tree line.
4474.m: The ibex and the chamois are often confused.

4480.q: How are wild leopards doing in the world today?
a: There are many more every year
4480.e: Leopards are considered threatened worldwide. They are losing habitat and are poached. Some subspecies are already very rare.

4489.q: You see a picture of a leopard with jet-black fur. What is it often called?
4489.e: A leopard with black fur is often called a black panther. In good light you can still faintly see its rosettes.
4489.m: The black panther is a leopard.

4500.q: What does it mean that leopards are mostly solitary?
a: They mostly live and hunt alone
They only live alone in zoos
4500.e: Adult leopards usually live alone and defend a territory. Only mothers with young go around together.

4514.q: Which animal has long, curved horns and climbs steep rocks in the Alps?
4514.e: The ibex lives high in the mountains and can climb steep rock faces thanks to its special hooves. The chamois climbs too, but has only short little horns. The ibex is the heraldic animal of the canton of the Grisons.
4514.m: The ibex climbs in the mountains.

4532.q: You would like something expensive. What is a sensible thing to do?
a: Put some money aside every week until you have enough
Borrow money from friends straight away
Empty a brother's or sister's piggy bank
Lie to your parents so they buy it
4532.e: If you regularly put a little money aside, over time you will have enough for what you want. This is called saving.
4532.m: Save step by step for what you want.

4542.q: What does the body mainly need vitamin C for?
a: For a strong immune system and healthy connective tissue
4542.e: Vitamin C supports the body's defences and is important for the skin and for healing wounds. The body cannot make it itself.
4542.m: Vitamin C strengthens your immune system.

a: Through very little precipitation over a long time
4558.e: Deserts are often in areas with particular wind patterns where hardly any rain clouds reach. That is why hardly any precipitation falls there for years.

4573.q: Which prey animals does the African wild dog often hunt?
4573.e: It hunts antelopes such as impalas and sometimes young wildebeest too. The prey depends on the area.
4573.m: Impalas and wildebeest are on the menu.

4599.q: What often happened to farms in communist countries?
a: They were merged into large state farms
They were sold to rich families
4599.e: In many communist countries, farmers had to give up their farms. The state then farmed the land collectively.
4599.m: Farms often belonged to the state.

4601.q: Which big railway town belongs to the canton of Solothurn?
4601.e: Olten is also in the canton of Solothurn and is known as an important railway junction. From there, trains go in many directions across Switzerland.
4601.m: Olten is an important railway town in the canton of Solothurn.

4608.q: Which family does the African wild dog belong to?
4608.e: It belongs to the dog family (Canidae). Despite its looks, it is not closely related to hyenas.
4608.m: Wild dogs belong to the dog family.

4642.q: What happens if more people say Yes than No in a vote?
a: The proposal is forgotten at once
4642.e: If there are more Yes votes than No votes when they are counted on voting Sunday, the proposal is accepted.
4642.m: If there are more Yes votes, the proposal is accepted.

4650.q: What is the main task of the UNHCR?
a: To protect and support refugees around the world
4650.e: The UNHCR is the refugee agency of the United Nations. It works to make sure that people who have fled get protection, shelter and rights.
4650.m: The UNHCR protects refugees around the world.

4674.q: What do you call animals that, like the wild dog, hunt and eat other animals?
4674.e: Predators feed on other animals that they hunt. The wild dog is one of them.

4703.q: Which gland in the neck controls the body's metabolism with hormones?
4703.e: The thyroid sits in the neck and produces hormones that control how the body uses energy. For this it needs iodine from food.

4722.q: Which animal is shown on the flag of Wales?
4722.e: The red dragon has been the symbol of Wales for centuries. It can be seen on the flag on a green and white background.

a: A dense, evergreen forest with lots of rain
A forest in the middle of the desert
4730.e: In tropical rainforests it rains a lot all year round. That is why especially many different plants and animals live there.
4730.m: In the rainforest it rains a lot all year.

4739.q: The brown trout is cold-blooded. What does that mean?
a: Its body temperature adjusts to the water
Its body temperature is always 37 degrees
4739.e: Cold-blooded animals produce hardly any heat of their own. When the water is cold, their body works more slowly.
4739.m: In the cold-blooded brown trout, body temperature adjusts to the water.

4777.q: What is the warm, dry wind called that blows down the mountainsides in the Swiss Alps?
4777.e: The föhn forms when moist air rises up a mountain range, drops its rain and sinks down dry on the other side. As it sinks, the air warms up a lot.
4777.m: The föhn is a warm wind from the mountains.

4784.q: How does a simple electromagnet work?
a: Electricity flows through a coil of wire and creates a magnetic field
A stone is heated until it becomes magnetic
Two mirrors are placed facing each other
Water is poured around a wire
4784.e: When electricity flows through a coiled wire, a magnetic field forms around it. If you switch the electricity off, the magnetic force disappears again.
4784.m: Electricity in a coil makes a magnet.

4796.q: What does the pulse you can feel at your wrist show?
a: How many times the heart beats per minute
4796.e: With every heartbeat a wave of blood flows through the arteries. You can feel and count this as your pulse.

4797.q: Which animal is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Schaffhausen?
4797.e: The coat of arms of Schaffhausen shows a black ram rearing up on a gold background. The town's name, though, actually comes from “Schiffshausen”, meaning boat houses.

4821.q: How do adult wild dogs often bring food to the pups?
a: They bring up meat for them
They put fruit in the nest
4821.e: The adults bring up half-digested meat. This way the pups and the guards at the den are fed too.
4821.m: The pack shares food with the young.

4825.q: In the photo you can see a spawning pit. How is it made?
a: The female beats a hollow in the gravel with her tail
Beavers dig it for the fish
The male builds it from twigs
It forms when rain churns up the stream
4825.e: The female beats a pit into the gravel bed with her tail. There she lays her eggs and then covers them up again.
4825.m: The female beats pits into the gravel.

4831.q: What is the aim of the agreement on the free movement of persons between Switzerland and the EU?
a: People can more easily work and live in Switzerland and the EU
4831.e: This agreement allows citizens of Switzerland and the EU to work, study or live more easily in each other’s countries. It is part of the bilateral agreements.
4831.m: Free movement makes it easier to work and live abroad.

4832.q: In a wild dog pack, who often gets to eat first?
4832.e: In wild dogs, the pups are often allowed to eat first. This is a special kind of social behaviour.
4832.m: In wild dogs, the young often eat first.

a: A rule that everyone must follow
4844.e: Laws are rules that apply to everyone in a country. They are decided by parliament or by the people.

4903.q: What do Christians celebrate at Easter?
a: The end of fasting in Islam
4903.e: At Easter Christians believe that Jesus came back to life after his death. It is one of the most important Christian festivals.
4903.m: Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus.

4911.q: What do you call people who help govern the municipality, the canton or the country?
4911.e: Politicians work in governments and parliaments. They make important decisions for everyone.
4911.m: Politicians make decisions for the community.

4942.q: In the photo, the brown trout can hardly be seen on the gravel bed. What is its colouring for?
4942.e: The colours and spots match the bottom of the stream. So the trout is hard to see and can take prey by surprise.

4967.q: Why does your face go red when you run fast?
a: More blood flows to the skin to give off heat
4967.e: When you run, you get warm. To get rid of the heat, more blood flows to the surface of the skin.
4967.m: Blood helps to cool you down.

4998.q: There are no lions or tigers in Sri Lanka. So what is the Sri Lankan leopard on the island?
a: The biggest wild cat on the island
An animal that only lives in zoos now
4998.e: Because there are no lions or tigers in Sri Lanka, the Sri Lankan leopard is the biggest wild cat on the island. It is at the top of the food chain.
4998.m: In Sri Lanka the leopard is the biggest wild cat.

5009.q: Besides water and light, what does a plant need to grow?
5009.e: Plants take important nutrients from the soil through their roots. Together with water and light they can then grow well.
5009.m: Plants need nutrients from the soil.

5012.q: Which organ produces bile for digesting fat and breaks down poisons?
5012.e: The liver is an important organ for removing poisons. It also produces bile, which helps to digest fat.
5012.m: The liver removes poisons from your body.

a: A brochure explaining the proposals being voted on
5016.e: Before every vote, the Confederation sends all voters a booklet with arguments from supporters and opponents.
5016.m: The booklet explains the pros and cons.

5017.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
5017.e: On 9 November 1989 the border between East and West Berlin opened. People celebrated at the Wall.

5018.q: Which country has a red maple leaf on its flag?
5018.e: The maple leaf is Canada's best-known symbol and has been on the flag since 1965. Maple trees grow there in huge forests.
5018.m: Canada has a red maple leaf.

5024.q: In a shop you are given too much change by mistake. What do you do?
a: I tell the shop assistant and give it back
I keep it and say nothing
I give it to a friend
5024.e: Honesty matters a lot with money. Money you receive by mistake should be given back.
5024.m: Honestly give back money you were given by mistake.

5042.q: Which water temperature does the brown trout like best?
a: Water that is frozen in winter
5042.e: The brown trout is a cold-water fish. If the water gets too warm, it gets stressed and there is too little oxygen.
5042.m: The brown trout is a cold-water fish.

5059.q: What do you call energy that is obtained from the power of the wind with large wind turbines?
5059.e: Wind drives the large blades of the wind turbines, which produces electricity. Because the wind never runs out, wind energy is a renewable energy.
5059.m: Wind turns the blades, and that makes electricity.

5064.q: What does a minimum size mean in fishing?
a: A minimum length a fish must reach before it may be caught
The lowest allowed weight of the fishing line
5064.e: Smaller fish must be put back gently into the water. That way they can grow and breed later.
5064.m: Fish that are too small stay in the water.

5083.q: What is the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, or OECD for short?
a: A group of countries that promotes the economy
5083.e: The OECD is made up of many economically strong countries, and Switzerland is also a member. It compares economic data and gives recommendations for better policies.
5083.m: The OECD promotes economic cooperation between states.

5088.q: Which material stops electricity flowing through a wire into your hand?
5088.e: Plastic does not conduct electricity, which is why cables are covered with it. This means you can touch them safely.

5116.q: What is the name of an area in the canton of Solothurn with many fields, close to the canton of Aargau?
5116.e: The Gäu lies in the canton of Solothurn near the border with the canton of Aargau. There are many fields and small villages there.

5120.q: Who founded the organisation called the Red Cross?
5120.e: The Swiss Henry Dunant founded the Red Cross in 1863 after he had seen wounded soldiers at a battle. He later received the first Nobel Peace Prize for it.
5120.m: Henry Dunant founded the Red Cross.

5140.e: A barometer measures air pressure, meaning how strongly the air presses down on the Earth. Changes in air pressure help to forecast the weather.

5146.q: What do you call a protected area where animals such as the wild dog live safely?
5146.e: In national parks, animals and their habitats are protected. Wild dogs can live there undisturbed too.
5146.m: National parks protect animals and habitats.

5170.q: What applies when young people under 18 sign a contract such as a mobile phone contract?
a: They usually need their parents' consent, because minors only have limited legal capacity
The contract is always automatically valid
Minors may not sign any contracts at all
The contract is only valid if it is made verbally
5170.e: In Switzerland minors have only limited legal capacity, so many contracts need their parents' consent. This protects young people from financial traps.

5172.q: Why do scientists give animals such as the brown trout a Latin name?
a: So that they have the same name all over the world
Because Latin is shorter than English
So that nobody understands the name
Because the animals come from Italy
5172.e: The brown trout has a different name in every language. But the Latin name Salmo trutta fario is used everywhere, so scientists worldwide know which animal is meant.
5172.m: Latin names are valid all over the world.

5178.q: Which physical changes are typical of puberty?
a: A growth spurt and the development of adult body features
5178.e: In puberty, hormones change the body into an adult body. This includes growth and physical changes.

5180.q: Roughly how old does a leopard get in the wild?
5180.e: In the wild, leopards usually live 12 to 17 years. In zoos they can live longer.
5180.m: Wild leopards live to about 15 years.

5185.q: When are African wild dogs usually active?
a: Mainly in the morning and evening
Only in the middle of the night
5185.e: They usually hunt in the cooler morning and evening hours. At midday they often rest in the shade.
5185.m: Wild dogs hunt at dawn and dusk.

5220.q: What is the difference between the EU and NATO?
a: The EU is an economic and political union, NATO a military defence alliance
The EU has a shared army, NATO does not
5220.e: The EU mainly promotes economic and political cooperation between its member states. NATO, on the other hand, is a military alliance whose members promise to help each other in case of attack. Switzerland belongs to neither.
5220.m: The EU is economic and political, NATO is military.

a: Only one party is allowed to govern.
Anyone may start their own party.
5233.e: In a one-party system only a single party is allowed. Other opinions and groups may not take part.
5233.m: Only one party has a say.

5249.q: How many gold stars are on the flag of the European Union?
5249.e: The EU flag always shows 12 gold stars in a circle, no matter how many countries are members. The number 12 stands for unity and completeness.
5249.m: The EU flag always has twelve stars.

5256.q: What is it called when cantons, parties and associations may give their views on a planned law before it goes to parliament?
5256.e: In the consultation procedure, different groups can comment on a draft law before it is debated in parliament.
5256.m: The consultation procedure collects opinions in advance.

5266.q: What is used to measure weather data high up in the atmosphere?
5266.e: Weather balloons carry instruments high up and send data on temperature, pressure and humidity to ground stations.
5266.m: Weather balloons measure data high up in the air.

a: An attempt by Czechoslovakia to make communism more humane, ended by Soviet troops
The start of communist rule in Czechoslovakia
A trade fair in Eastern Europe
5273.e: Under Alexander Dubček, Czechoslovakia tried to reform socialism. Warsaw Pact troops ended this attempt with an invasion.
5273.m: The Prague Spring was an attempt at reform that was crushed.

a: Newspapers may write what really happens.
5281.e: With a free press, journalists may report the truth even if the government doesn’t like it. In dictatorships this is often forbidden.
5281.m: A free press reports the truth.

5283.q: How does the moon change its appearance in the sky over a month?
5283.e: The moon does not shine by itself; we only see the part lit by the sun. That is why the moon sometimes looks like a crescent and sometimes completely round.
5283.m: The moon changes shape every month.

5290.q: What is the procedure for resolving differences?
a: The National Council and the Council of States bring their different decisions on a law into line
5290.e: If the National Council and the Council of States disagree on a law, the proposal is sent back and forth until they reach agreement. This is called resolving differences.
5290.m: Resolving differences settles disagreements between the chambers.

5291.q: Why is it a good idea to look at prices when shopping with your parents?
a: So you learn how much things cost and shop thoughtfully
Because the shop staff require it
Because otherwise you will be punished
5291.e: If you pay attention to prices, you learn what things are worth and can make more thoughtful decisions. This helps later when you run your own household.
5291.m: Looking at prices helps you learn.

5322.q: What are price comparison websites useful for?
a: To compare prices or services of different providers before buying or signing up
To automatically choose the most expensive offer
5322.e: Comparison websites show different offers side by side clearly, for example for insurance or mobile phone contracts. This makes it easier to find a cheap offer that suits you.

a: The distance light travels in one year
The time a planet takes to go round once
An especially bright year for astronomers
The time between two solar eclipses
5345.e: A light year is a unit of distance, not of time, and is about 9.5 trillion kilometres. It is used to make the huge distances in space easier to understand.
5345.m: A light year measures distance, not time.

5352.q: You see a leopard and a cheetah. How can you recognise the cheetah?
a: By the black tear stripes on its face
5352.e: Cheetahs have black lines running from the eyes to the mouth and simple spots on their fur. Leopards have rosettes.
5352.m: The cheetah has tear stripes on its face, the leopard has rosettes in its fur.

5386.q: Which animal is an enemy that often tries to take the wild dogs' prey?
5386.e: Lions and spotted hyenas sometimes steal the wild dogs' prey. Lions can also kill wild dogs.
5386.m: Lions and hyenas are rivals of wild dogs.

5401.q: What is the basic principle of a generator?
a: It converts kinetic energy into electricity using magnetic fields
It stores chemical energy in a cell
It produces light by heating a wire
It turns electricity directly into water
5401.e: If a coil of wire is turned in a magnetic field, a voltage is produced in it. Generators in power stations use exactly this principle to produce electricity.
5401.m: Movement in a magnetic field produces electricity.

a: A famine in Ukraine in the 1930s partly caused by the Soviet government
A festival celebrating the October Revolution
A trade agreement between East and West
5414.e: In the early 1930s, millions of people in Ukraine died in a famine. It was made much worse by the forced collectivisation of farming and Stalin’s policies.
5414.m: The Holodomor was a famine in Ukraine.

5429.q: What does the World Trade Organization (WTO), based in Geneva, do?
a: It sets rules for international trade
5429.e: The WTO makes sure there are shared trade rules between countries and settles trade disputes. Its headquarters are in Geneva.

5467.q: How successful are African wild dogs at hunting compared with lions?
5467.e: Wild dogs are among the most successful hunters in Africa. Their teamwork and stamina pay off.
5467.m: Wild dogs are very successful hunters.

5497.q: What is the person called who calls people to prayer from the minaret?
5497.e: The muezzin calls out the call to prayer five times a day. In the past he climbed the minaret to do it; today loudspeakers are often used.
5497.m: The muezzin calls people to prayer.

5508.e: The brain sits protected inside your skull. It controls everything you think, feel and do.
5508.m: Your brain lives in your head.

5514.q: What does freedom of expression mean?
a: You may say openly what you think.
You must always agree with the government.
You may only talk at home.
5514.e: Freedom of expression means that everyone may express their thoughts freely without being punished. In dictatorships this is often not allowed.
5514.m: Freedom of expression allows open speech.

a: Energy obtained from the heat inside the Earth
Energy from the movement of the seas
Energy from the Earth's magnetic field
5552.e: Deep inside the Earth it is very hot. This heat can be used to heat houses or to produce electricity.
5552.m: Geothermal energy uses heat from the Earth.

a: An important leader of the October Revolution who was later exiled by Stalin
The founder of the Berlin Wall
5553.e: Leon Trotsky played a major part in organising the Red Army and the Revolution of 1917. Later Stalin drove him out of the Soviet Union, and he was murdered in Mexico in 1940.
5553.m: Trotsky was later exiled by Stalin.

5564.q: Which organ stores extra sugar as glycogen?
5564.e: The liver stores glucose in the form of glycogen. When needed, it turns it back into sugar for energy.
5564.m: The liver stores sugar as glycogen.

5570.q: What happens to an ice cube when you hold it in your hand?
a: It melts because of your body heat
5570.e: Your hand is warmer than the ice, so it gives heat to the ice. This turns the solid ice into liquid water.

5581.q: What do you call a group of African wild dogs?
5581.e: Wild dogs live in packs. A pack usually consists of related animals.
5581.m: Wild dogs live in a pack.

5585.q: Why do cacti have spines instead of large leaves?
5585.e: Large leaves lose a lot of water through evaporation. Cacti live in dry areas, and thanks to their spines they save precious water.

5645.q: What protects your teeth on the outside?
5645.e: Tooth enamel is the hard outer layer of the teeth. It is even harder than bone.

5658.q: What is the force called that always pulls you towards the ground?
5658.e: The Earth's gravity pulls everything downwards. That is why things fall when you let go of them.

5662.q: Which big cat is the only one that usually lives in groups called prides?
5662.e: Lions live in prides with several females, their young and one or a few males. Tigers, leopards and jaguars are loners.
5662.m: The lion is the only big cat that lives in a pride.

5672.q: Which trout originally comes from North America and is now often kept on fish farms?
5672.e: The rainbow trout was brought to Europe from North America. It grows quickly and is therefore often farmed. Brown trout, lake trout and sea trout are native here.
5672.m: The rainbow trout comes from North America.

5676.q: What is the difference between a popular initiative and a referendum?
a: With an initiative you ask for something new, with a referendum you oppose a law that has been passed
Initiatives only apply to cantons, referendums only to municipalities
5676.e: With a popular initiative, the people ask for a new article in the constitution. With a referendum, the people can still stop a law passed by parliament.
5676.m: An initiative demands, a referendum brakes.

5688.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult African wild dog get?
5688.e: It is about as heavy as a medium-sized dog. The animals are slim and long-legged.
5688.m: Wild dogs weigh about 20 to 30 kilograms.

a: A strong thinning of the protective ozone layer, mainly over Antarctica
A hole in the Earth’s crust
5715.e: Certain chemicals have greatly weakened the ozone layer over Antarctica. As a result, more dangerous UV radiation reaches the Earth.
5715.m: The ozone hole weakens the atmosphere’s UV protection.

5722.q: The picture shows a habitat. Where does the brown trout feel most at home?
a: In a cool, clear stream with lots of oxygen
In a swamp with no current
5722.e: The brown trout needs clean, cold water rich in oxygen. It finds such conditions in fast-flowing streams.
5722.m: It loves cool, clear, fast streams.

5726.q: What does a seed need in order to germinate?
5726.e: A seed needs moisture and warmth to start sprouting. In the soil it also finds support and nutrients.
5726.m: Seeds need water, warmth and soil.

5745.q: What do Buddhist monks and nuns often do to find inner peace?
5745.e: When meditating, Buddhist monks and nuns sit still and concentrate on their breathing. In this way they try to calm their thoughts.
5745.m: Meditation helps you find inner peace.

a: The vote of a canton when counting the majority of cantons
The vote of a single citizen
A second vote for Swiss living abroad
5746.e: In votes that need a majority of the cantons, the result in each canton counts as one cantonal vote. The six former half-cantons, such as Obwalden or Basel-Stadt, each have half a cantonal vote.
5746.m: Each canton has one cantonal vote.

5749.q: How many pups are often in an African wild dog litter?
a: Often more than six, sometimes over ten
5749.e: Wild dogs have quite large litters. The number of pups can even be over ten.

5758.e: Fish eggs are called roe. Milt is the name for the males' sperm.

5807.q: Which country has a red circle in the middle of a white flag?
5807.e: The red circle on the Japanese flag represents the rising sun. That is why Japan is also called the “Land of the Rising Sun”.
5807.m: Japan's flag shows a red sun.

5843.q: What is special about the African wild dog's paws compared with many other dogs?
a: They have four toes on the front paws
5843.e: The wild dog has no fifth toe, the so-called dewclaw, on its front paws. So it has four toes there.
5843.m: Wild dogs have only four toes at the front.

a: Being unable to digest milk sugar properly
5849.e: With lactose intolerance, an enzyme for digesting milk sugar is missing. This often leads to tummy ache after dairy products.
5849.m: With lactose intolerance, milk sugar is hard to digest.

a: Restructuring the economy with more freedom for businesses
5868.e: Perestroika means ‘restructuring’. Gorbachev wanted to reform the weak Soviet economy with it, which in the end also led to big political changes.
5868.m: Perestroika meant restructuring the Soviet economy.

5875.q: What is a treaty between two countries?
a: A written agreement that both keep to
5875.e: In a treaty, countries promise, for example, to work together or to avoid disputes. Such treaties are very important for peace.
5875.m: A treaty is an agreement between countries.

5881.q: What does the African wild dog mainly eat?
5881.e: It is a meat-eater and mainly hunts medium-sized antelopes such as impalas. Smaller prey is also on the menu.
5881.m: Wild dogs are meat-eaters and hunt antelopes.

5898.q: What is the name of the beautiful old castle with a large garden near Solothurn?
5898.e: Waldegg Castle stands on a hill near Feldbrunnen and was built long ago for a rich gentleman. Today you can visit the beautiful garden and the rooms.
5898.m: Waldegg Castle stands on a hill near Solothurn.

a: A question from members of parliament to the Federal Council, which it must answer
A law about Swiss living abroad
5900.e: With an interpellation, members of parliament can ask the government for information. The Federal Council must then answer these questions in writing.
5900.m: An interpellation asks the Federal Council for information.

5903.q: What does ‘cumulating’ mean in an election?
a: Writing a name twice on the ballot paper
5903.e: When cumulating, you give a person twice the weight by writing their name twice. This way the person gets more votes.
5903.m: Cumulating doubles the vote for one person.

5908.q: What makes the wild dog a good long-distance runner?
5908.e: It can chase its prey over long distances. This tires out the prey animals.
5908.m: Wild dogs hunt with lots of stamina.

5916.q: What is the so-called ‘magic formula’ in Swiss politics?
a: A fixed sharing of Federal Council seats among the largest parties
The name of the Federal Constitution
5916.e: The magic formula describes how the seats on the Federal Council are traditionally shared among the largest parties.
5916.m: The magic formula shares out Federal Council seats.

5932.q: Where is the asteroid belt in our solar system?
a: Between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter
Between the Earth and the moon
5932.e: The asteroid belt contains countless rocks of different sizes. It lies between the orbit of Mars and the orbit of Jupiter.
5932.m: The asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter.

5940.q: You see a brown trout. Which family of fish does it belong to?
5940.e: The brown trout belongs to the salmon family. Its relatives include the salmon and the rainbow trout.
5940.m: The brown trout is in the salmon family.

5956.q: What is one difference between a leopard and a jaguar?
a: The jaguar is more powerfully built
The leopard lives in South America
5956.e: The jaguar looks bulkier and has a bigger head. It also lives in America, while the leopard lives in Africa and Asia.
5956.m: The jaguar is stockier, the leopard slimmer.

5979.q: What shape is our galaxy, the Milky Way?
a: A flat disc with no structure
5979.e: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy with several arms winding round a centre. Our solar system is in one of these arms.
5979.m: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy.

5988.q: What is the layer called that protects the Earth from dangerous UV radiation?
5988.e: The ozone layer is high up in the atmosphere and filters out a large part of the sun’s harmful UV radiation. Without it, life on Earth would be much harder.
5988.m: The ozone layer protects against UV radiation.

6009.q: In the photo a leopard is lying on a branch. What does it often do with its prey in the tree?
a: It hides it and eats it there
It throws it into the water
6009.e: Leopards are strong climbers and drag their prey up trees. This protects it from lions and hyenas.
6009.m: Leopards take their prey up trees.

6011.q: Why is it important that all adults are allowed to have a say?
a: So that decisions are fair for everyone
So that there are more holidays
So that nobody has to work
So that everyone looks the same
6011.e: When many people are allowed to help decide, decisions become fairer. Every vote counts the same.

a: Signals are passed from one nerve cell to the next
6023.e: At the synapse, a nerve cell uses messenger substances to pass a signal to the next cell. This is how communication in the nervous system works.

6056.q: What is the Federal Constitution, explained very simply?
6056.e: The Federal Constitution contains the most important rules about how Switzerland is organised. It can only be changed by the people.
6056.m: The constitution is the most important rule book.

6062.q: What is the protein in red blood cells that picks up and carries oxygen called?
6062.e: Haemoglobin contains iron and picks up oxygen in the lungs. It also gives blood its red colour.

6069.q: Which language, besides English, is often also spoken at many international conferences?
6069.e: Besides English, French is one of the most important languages at international meetings, partly because Geneva is a French-speaking city. The UN has six official languages in total.
6069.m: French is often an important conference language.

6080.q: Who began a period of ‘de-Stalinisation’ after Stalin’s death?
6080.e: In 1956 Nikita Khrushchev criticised Stalin’s crimes in a famous speech. After that, some rules in the Soviet Union were relaxed a little.

6112.q: What does a torch need to shine?
6112.e: The battery supplies the electricity that makes the small bulb or LED light up. Without electricity the torch stays dark.
6112.m: No torch shines without a battery.

6116.q: What does a secret police do in a dictatorship?
a: It secretly watches people who think differently.
6116.e: A secret police searches in secret for people who criticise the ruler. This makes many people afraid, and they no longer dare to speak freely.
6116.m: Secret police secretly watch the people.

6121.q: Which animal is the national symbol and heraldic animal of the USA?
6121.e: The bald eagle was declared the national symbol of the USA in 1782 and appears on the country's Great Seal. It stands for strength and freedom.
6121.m: The USA has the bald eagle as its symbol.

6133.q: How does a male leopard usually differ from a female?
a: It has stripes instead of spots
6133.e: Male leopards are usually much heavier than females. They can weigh about 60 to 90 kilograms.

a: A state insurance that pays a pension in old age and is partly funded by working people
A private savings insurance for children
A health insurance for young people
6138.e: AHV (old-age and survivors' insurance) is Switzerland's state pension insurance. All working people pay into it during their working life so that pensions can be paid out later.
6138.m: AHV provides a pension in old age.

6143.q: What is the Hindu place of worship called?
6143.e: In a Hindu temple there are statues of different gods. People pray there and bring flowers and offerings.

6160.q: Which part of the body helps you grab and hold things?
6160.e: With your fingers you can grab, hold and feel things. Your hand is very skilful.

a: A disease in which bones lose density
A vision problem in old age
6161.e: With osteoporosis the bones lose density and break more easily. Older people in particular are affected more often.
6161.m: Osteoporosis makes bones break more easily.

6163.q: How can you tell individual leopards apart in camera trap pictures?
a: By the spot pattern, which is different for each one
By the size of their ears
By the colour of their eyes
6163.e: Every leopard's spot pattern is unique, a bit like a fingerprint. Researchers use this to count the animals.

6176.q: What do bees collect from flowers?
6176.e: Bees fly from flower to flower and suck up the sweet nectar. In doing so they help the plants to reproduce.

a: The group that runs a country, a canton or a municipality
6183.e: A government makes important decisions and makes sure laws are carried out. In Switzerland there are governments at federal, cantonal and municipal level.
6183.m: The government runs the country, canton or municipality.

6189.q: Is the snow leopard a subspecies of the leopard?
a: No, it is a separate species
Yes, a subspecies from the Himalayas
Yes, a subspecies with light fur
No, it belongs to the lynxes
6189.e: The snow leopard is called Panthera uncia and is a separate species. It is related to the leopard, but it is not the same animal. It is not a lynx either.
6189.m: The snow leopard is a separate species.

6203.e: Leopards usually hunt at dusk and at night. During the day they often rest in the shade or in trees.

6217.q: Because of its coat, what else is the African wild dog called?
6217.e: The name hyena dog comes from its spotted appearance and its hunched walk, which is reminiscent of hyenas. But it is not related to hyenas.
6217.m: Hyena dog is another name for it.

6230.q: What is the force called that keeps an aeroplane in the air when it flies?
6230.e: The shape of the wings makes the air flow faster over the wings than underneath. This creates a difference in pressure that carries the aeroplane upwards.
6230.m: Lift keeps the aeroplane in the air.

6236.q: In which part of Africa does the African wild dog mainly live today?
a: In the middle of the Sahara
6236.e: The African wild dog lives mainly in the savannahs south of the Sahara, for example in Botswana, Tanzania and Zimbabwe. Today it is only found in small areas.
6236.m: The wild dog lives in Africa's savannahs south of the Sahara.

6267.q: What do you usually hear shortly after a flash of lightning?
6267.e: Lightning and thunder happen at the same time, but light is much faster than sound. That is why you see the lightning first and only hear the thunder afterwards.
6267.m: After the lightning comes the thunder.

6270.q: What is the main colour of the United Nations flag?
6270.e: The UN flag shows a map of the world on a light blue background. The colour stands for peace.
6270.m: The UN flag is light blue with a map of the world.

6273.q: What is the name of the well-known monastery in the canton of Solothurn that many pilgrims visit?
6273.e: Mariastein Abbey lies in the canton of Solothurn near the border with Basel and France. Many people make pilgrimages there because it has a famous chapel of grace.
6273.m: Mariastein Abbey is in the canton of Solothurn.

6281.q: Which material does light shine through well?
6281.e: Glass is transparent, so light gets through almost unhindered. Wood or stone blocks the light.
6281.m: Glass lets light through, stone does not.

6327.q: What does the Antarctic Treaty lay down?
a: That Antarctica may only be used for peaceful and scientific purposes
That only Switzerland may do research in Antarctica
That Antarctica will be sold to a single country
That wars may be fought in Antarctica
6327.e: Several states agreed to keep Antarctica free of military activity and to use it only for research. The treaty shows how countries can make rules for an area together.
6327.m: Antarctica is for peace and research.

6338.q: Why do you slip more easily on a smooth wooden floor in socks than in trainers?
a: The friction between socks and floor is smaller
6338.e: The rubber sole of trainers grips the floor well. Smooth fabric on smooth wood creates only a little friction, so you slip easily.

6348.q: Which animals are the “Big Five” in Africa?
6348.e: The Big Five are the lion, leopard, elephant, rhino and buffalo. They used to be seen as especially hard to hunt; today they are mostly photographed.
6348.m: The leopard is one of the Big Five.
